content.p: What I left out - and how it would grow

li.p: No DB engine - in-memory repository: right for an exercise, wrong for production; the swap point is one interface.
No merchant authentication - out of scope, documented in SOLUTION.md.
No retry scheduler / reconciliation job - the state machine already leaves the hook: INIT plus the idempotency key.
No circuit breaker - one bank, one instance; timeouts already cap the damage.
Tokenize card data, then move to real persistence - RDBMS with the same unique key.
Reconciliation job: sweep INIT records and ask the bank for late answers.
Circuit breaker plus scheduled retry with backoff.
Async via an event stream once consumers exist - the context pattern survives the move.

content.p: Equally important as what I built is what I did not, and why. There is no database engine - the repository is in-memory, which is correct for this exercise; in production, persistence is the first swap, and the interface already isolates it. No merchant authentication, no retry scheduler, no circuit breaker - each is documented as out of scope or unnecessary at this size. And I keep the evolution path explicit: tokenization first, then reconciliation over INIT records, then circuit breaking, then async once there are consumers.
